html:
The Holocaust in Hungary peaked in 1944, when Hungarian police and German officials deported about 437,000 Jews to Auschwitz in under two months. Most were killed on arrival.

German troops had occupied Hungary in March.

Hungary had passed anti-Jewish laws from 1938 and sent Jewish men to deadly labour service, but most of its Jews were alive in early 1944. Adolf Eichmann and Hungarian officials then emptied the countryside from May to July. Regent Horthy stopped the deportations in July, before those from Budapest. When the Arrow Cross fascists took power in October, they shot thousands of Jews into the Danube. Diplomats such as Raoul Wallenberg saved tens of thousands with protective passes. In all about 565,000 Hungarian Jews died in the Holocaust.
sum: The Holocaust in Hungary peaked in 1944, when Hungarian police and German officials deported about 437,000 Jews to Auschwitz in under two months. Most were killed on arrival.
